# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 31 (Bu-Vb Sk31)

**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sakkacca Sutta* constitutes the thirty-first training rule of the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic mealtime deportment and is rendered by Bhikkhu Brahmali as *Not eating respectfully* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists three modern translations in three languages, including the English translation by Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels for this rule appear widely across early Buddhist monastic codes [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels are found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bu-pm-sk31), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (pli-tv-bi-vb-sk31), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bi-pm-sk31), and both the *Bhikkhu* and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Outside the Pali lineage, full parallels exist in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit witnesses of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya (e.g., Lzh Mu Bu Vb Sk 46, xct-mu-bu-vb-sk48, and Sanskrit Prātimokṣa manuscripts) and an Upāliparipṛcchā translation [SuttaCentral]. Resembling regulations on respectful receipt and consumption of almsfood (*Sakkaccapaṭiggahaṇa*) are found in the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṅghika traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects 105 Pali-internal reuse passages across 46 texts, reflecting standard formulaic phrasing shared predominantly with other Sekhiya rules, particularly Sekhiya 35 (Bu-Vb Sk35, §0.1–1.14 ↔ §0.1–1.15), Sekhiya 33, Sekhiya 34, and Sekhiya 27, while recording no cross-language matches above the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
